title_html: Draft a company name using the pattern [City] + [Brand] + [Industry] + Co., Ltd.

items_html: The legal format is strict—e.g. Shanghai Acme CAD Design Co., Ltd.
Final name approval is part of filing; your agent can pre-check availability.

title_html: Find only commercial office space—residential units cannot be a WFOE address.

detail.html: Zoning must allow business registration; verify with your agent before you sign.

title_html: Get the landlord’s red Property Ownership Certificate (or equivalent) for the filing.

detail.html: Without this document, the AMR typically rejects the application.

title_html: Sign the commercial lease (deposits often paid personally or by your offshore parent).

detail.html: The tenant may not exist on paper yet; after incorporation and chops, the WFOE may reimburse allowable pre-establishment costs—confirm with your agent and accountant.

title_html: Retain a corporate services firm (WFOE registration agent) with a written scope—AMR filing, chops, and optional bank / bookkeeping support.

items_html: Chinese law does not universally require a foreign founder to use an agent, but AMR online portals, templates, and local practice are almost entirely in Chinese—most overseas investors hire a firm to draft articles, run the AMR package, and coordinate chops and bank KYC.
Compare quotes before you finalize notarized / apostille packs: “incorporation only” vs. full-service (bank onboarding, bookkeeping, annual compliance).
Government AMR filing charges are usually modest; the main cash outlay here is professional service fees.

title_html: Notarize your passport or parent-company documents with a notary in your home country (e.g. a U.S. Notary Public is typical for U.S. passport holders).

detail.html: Individual investor = passport; corporate parent = entity docs—your agent will list exactly what is needed.

title_html: Obtain an Apostille from your country’s designated Hague authority (e.g. a U.S. state Secretary of State for documents originating in the United States).

detail.html: You no longer need Chinese Embassy legalization for this path—the Apostille is the standard certification.

title_html: Set registered capital and pay-in schedule in the articles—do not wire equity yet.

items_html: Registered capital (注册资本) is the subscribed total on the license; it is not the same as annual rent or payroll.
Under PRC Company Law (revised 1 Jul 2024), full pay-in within five years of establishment unless transition rules apply for older companies.
Choose amount using: minimum viable for your sector, business plan, license minimums, banking credibility, and repatriation plans—align with your accountant.
Employer social insurance + housing fund is separate from this line—see step 9 and the dashboard.

title_html: Model a 12-month budget: rent, agents, payroll, and statutory “five insurances + fund.”

items_html: Pre-WFOE costs (lease, travel) often come from personal or parent funds; reimbursement after setup may be possible—confirm with your agent.
Payroll + statutory is usually the largest variable for a CAD shop—use the dashboard.
Assume onshore operating cash in China after capital injection (steps 17–18) and revenue.

title_html: Name Legal Rep, Executive Director, and Supervisor—two roles cannot be the same person.

detail.html: The Supervisor cannot be the Legal Representative or Director. These names go into articles and bank mandates.

title_html: File the incorporation package with the AMR (lease + apostille + articles).

detail.html: Submit to the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR): lease, apostilled identity/parent docs, articles (capital, pay-in schedule, roles), and other required company rules.

title_html: Collect your Business License (营业执照)—the company legally exists.

detail.html: You still have no operational corporate bank accounts until steps 14–15.

title_html: Register and carve your company chops (official + financial seals).

detail.html: PSB + licensed vendor. A red chop on a contract is often decisive—secure storage; whoever holds chops controls signing.

title_html: Open the RMB basic deposit account (基本户) with license + chops.

detail.html: Main RMB account for salaries, rent, and tax—often the only account that can pay cash salaries. KYC applies.

title_html: Open the foreign-investment capital account for inbound equity (FCY).

detail.html: Name varies by bank (FDI / capital account). Pairs with SAFE registration of the foreign-invested enterprise.

title_html: Prepare the bank’s capital-contribution / FX forms with your agent (投资款 wording).

detail.html: The remittance must be coded as registered capital—not an informal “transfer.” Codes differ by bank.

title_html: Wire registered capital from abroad in foreign currency to the designated inbound account.

detail.html: Bank records paid-in capital (实缴) toward SAFE filing; obtain FX settlement documents. Multiple tranches allowed within five-year pay-in (step 8).

title_html: Settle FX (资本金结汇) and move RMB into the basic account for operations.

detail.html: Follow the bank’s process; this is company capital settlement, not personal remittance.

title_html: Register with the tax bureau and obtain fapiao (official invoicing) capability.

detail.html: You need this to bill customers compliantly on the mainland.

title_html: Register for social insurance—then you can hire and run payroll.

detail.html: Mandatory contributions are paid from the RMB basic account, funded by capital (steps 17–18) and revenue. Compare cities on the dashboard.
